helpCenter.content:
Starting July 1, 2026, the statutory minimum wage in the Netherlands will increase. To remain compliant, employers must ensure any team member employed in the Netherlands is paid at least the new minimum wage.

This draft summarizes the updated minimum wage amounts, how holiday allowance impacts the thresholds, and what this means for employers using Remote.

Who this applies to

This update applies to:

  • Employers with team members employed in the Netherlands through Remote Employer of Record (EOR)
  • Team members in the Netherlands whose salary is at or below the statutory minimum wage thresholds

What’s changing (effective July 1, 2026)

Minimum wage thresholds (40-hour workweek)

Adults (standard threshold)

  • Annual minimum wage (excluding holiday allowance): €31,299.12
  • Annual minimum wage (including holiday allowance): €33,803.05
  • Monthly minimum wage (excluding holiday allowance): €2,608.26
  • Monthly minimum wage (including holiday allowance): €2,816.92

19-year-old threshold

  • Annual minimum wage (excluding holiday allowance): €18,771.12
  • Annual minimum wage (including holiday allowance): €20,272.81
  • Monthly minimum wage (excluding holiday allowance): €1,564.26
  • Monthly minimum wage (including holiday allowance): €1,689.40

20-year-old threshold

  • Annual minimum wage (excluding holiday allowance): €25,035.12
  • Annual minimum wage (including holiday allowance): €27,037.93
  • Monthly minimum wage (excluding holiday allowance): €2,086.26
  • Monthly minimum wage (including holiday allowance): €2,253.16

How holiday allowance affects the minimum wage thresholds

In the Netherlands, it’s common for holiday allowance to be handled in one of two ways:

  • Included in the salary (the gross annual/monthly salary already includes holiday allowance), or
  • Paid on top of the base salary (holiday allowance is paid in addition to the base salary)

When comparing a salary to the minimum wage thresholds:

  • If holiday allowance is included, compare to the “including holiday allowance” threshold.
  • If holiday allowance is paid on top, compare the base salary to the “excluding holiday allowance” threshold.

What this means for employers using Remote

If a team member’s salary is below the new statutory minimum wage threshold, a salary update will be required to remain compliant.

Depending on the situation, Remote may also issue updated documentation for the team member (for example, a salary increase notification letter or other contract update documentation).

Part time employees

For part time employees, the minimum wage is prorated based on the contracted hours relative to the 40-hour standard workweek. An employee working 32 hours out of 40 is entitled to 80% of the full time minimum wage threshold. The same holiday allowance logic applies after prorating.

Does holiday allowance count toward the 30% ruling salary threshold?

Yes. The 30% ruling has a minimum salary requirement set by Dutch law each year. For 2026, this is €48,013 gross per year, or €36,497 for employees under 30 with a master's degree. Holiday allowance is part of the total fiscal annual salary, so it counts toward meeting this threshold. Payroll calculates this cumulatively across the year, using a year to date method. This works the same way whether holiday allowance is paid out monthly or as a lump sum in May.
helpCenter.title: Holiday allowance and minimum wage thresholds in the Netherlands

helpCenter.content:
In the Netherlands, we strongly encourage initially engaging employees on a fixed-term
contract of over 6 months and up to 12 months. This duration ensures sufficient time to
find a suitable match before committing to an indefinite contract and allows for the
implementation of a probation period.

During the probation period, termination can occur without consent from the court or the
UWV (the Dutch Employee Insurance Agency). Once the probation period ends, terminating
an employee does require consent. It's important to note that probation periods are not
valid in fixed-term contracts lasting 6 months or less.

For roles that are eligible for commission (such as sales roles), we recommend a
fixed-term employment agreement of over 6 months, which includes a 1-month probation
period.

Indefinite term contracts

Under Dutch law, indefinite term employment contracts come with certain risks:

  • Employees on sick leave receive salary for up to two years, and termination during
    this period is generally prohibited, making mutual terminations rare and costly
  • Due to robust unfair dismissal protections, terminating employees beyond their
    probation period requires approval from either the court or the UWV (the Dutch
    Employee Insurance Agency)
  • The law favors employees and necessitates extensive proof, making settlement a common
    and costly outcome

What if an extension of fixed-term contract is needed?

If an extension is needed, the fixed-term contract may be extended for a second or third
period of up to 12 months, a common practice in the Netherlands. A fixed-term employment
agreement automatically converts to an indefinite one upon its third renewal or if it
the total duration of all fixed-term agreements exceeds 36 months, whichever happens
earlier.

 

Differences between the 2 contract types

1. Fixed-Term contract

  • Limited to a specific period, typically 6 to 12 months
  • Ends automatically at the end of the term without the need for termination
  • Probation periods are not valid for contracts of 6 months or less
  • Can be renewed, but automatically converts to an indefinite one upon its third
    renewal or if it the total duration of all fixed-term agreements exceeds 36 months,
    whichever happens earlier

2. Indefinite contract

  • No end date
  • Termination requires consent from the court or the Dutch Employee Insurance Agency
    (UWV) for termination after the probation period
  • Probation period can be added. During the probation period, termination can occur
    without consent from the court or the UWV (the Dutch Employee Insurance Agency)
  • Renewal is not applicable as the contract does not have a fixed end date
helpCenter.title: Contract duration in the Netherlands

statement.description:

For this reason, we recommend you engage employees on a fixed term agreement of 7 to 12 months in the first instance and utilise the maximum fixed term agreements thereafter.

Why a minimum of 7 months? Because we also recommend including a probation period and probation periods are not valid in fixed term agreements of 6 months or less.

helpCenter.callToAction: Learn more about equity management at Remote
helpCenter.content:
Remote Equity is a lightweight compliance tool designed to help you manage equity grants across borders for team members hired through Remote's Employer of Record (EOR).

Whether you’re managing vesting, reporting exercises, or navigating local tax laws, Remote Equity gives you the structure to stay compliant, avoid risk, and support your team across borders.

Why it matters

As your EOR, Remote is legally responsible for equity-related tax and reporting in the countries where your team members are employed. That means we don’t just track equity, we:

  • Withhold and report taxes when required
  • File with local tax authorities
  • Support team members with clear guidance on their tax responsibilities

Most equity platforms can’t do that because they’re not the legal employer. Remote Equity ensures we have the data we need, when we need it, to keep your company compliant and your team fairly rewarded.

Behind the scenes, our tax team:

  • Handles tax withholdings when taxable events occur
  • Provides guidance to you and your team, even when no withholding is required
  • Manages additional reporting where local laws demand it

See also: What types of equity grants should I declare in Remote Equity?

What’s included

Remote Equity provides:

  • Tracking and alerts for events that may create a tax obligation (like vesting or exercising)
  • Automated compliance reminders based on local deadlines and regulations
  • Localized guidance for team members, shared through the Remote Equity app
  • Support from Remote’s tax and legal teams, who handle obligations on your behalf
  • Integration with Carta and Pulley to automatically sync grant declarations and exercise information

Get started in minutes

Setup takes less than five minutes. Just log in to your Remote account, and launch the Equity App to follow the setup steps.

Helpful guides to get started:

  • How can I access Remote Equity?
  • How do I declare a grant?
  • How can my team access their equity information?
  • What happens if I already declared equity before using Remote Equity?

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Who needs to use Remote Equity?

Any Remote customer granting equity to a team member hired through Remote’s EOR must use Remote Equity to meet local compliance requirements.

Why can’t we just use our own equity tool?

Traditional equity tools track grants and vesting, but they don't file taxes, withhold contributions, or report income to local authorities. Remote, as the legal employer, is responsible for these actions. Remote Equity ensures those obligations are covered.

What happens if we don’t use it?

If Remote doesn’t receive timely and accurate equity data, required filings may be missed. This can result in compliance risks, unexpected tax liabilities, and issues for both your company and your team members.

How much does Remote Equity cost?

Remote Equity costs 39 USD per month for each EOR team member with equity. Learn more.

For comprehensive information, visit the Remote Equity hub.
helpCenter.title: Welcome to Remote Equity: Global equity, without the compliance headaches

helpCenter.content:
For the Netherlands, Remote recommends selecting the longest probation period duration possible for the fixed contract length.

Limitations for probationary periods

Maximum Duration:

  • Indefinite Contracts (Permanent Contracts):
    • Maximum probation period: Two months.
  • Fixed-Term Contracts:
    • Contracts of six months or less: No probation period is allowed.
    • Contracts longer than six months but less than two years: Maximum probation period is one month.
    • Contracts of two years or more: Maximum probation period is two months.

Mutual Agreement:

  • The probation period must be the same for both the employer and the employee.
  • It must be explicitly stated in the written contract or appointment letter.

Immediate Termination:

  • During the probation period, both parties can terminate the employment contract with immediate effect without providing a reason.

Notice Periods

  • The notice period is typically one month unless otherwise agreed in the contract, with a maximum notice period of six months for both employer and employee. The exact duration must be the same for both parties unless otherwise stated in a collective labor agreement (CAO).

Additional Protections

  • Collective Labor Agreements (CAO):
    • Collective labor agreements can set different rules regarding probation periods and contract duration, provided they comply with the minimum legal standards.
  • Employee Rights:
    • Employees on fixed-term contracts have similar rights to those on indefinite contracts, including rights to sick leave, holiday allowance, and protection against unfair dismissal.

These rules ensure a balance between the flexibility for employers to assess the suitability of new employees and the security and rights of employees within the Dutch labor market.

 

Disclaimer: Please be advised that the information provided is for general guidance only and should not be considered legal advice. Clients are strongly encouraged to contact the Lifecycle Contracts Management Team for expert guidance and assistance in navigating the intricate landscape of employee documentation requirements in Netherlands. Consulting with our Lifecycle Contracts Management Team is imperative to ensure compliance with local employment standards legislation. Your proactive engagement with our Lifecycle Contracts Management Team is vital to making informed decisions and adhering to all relevant regulations.

In the Netherlands, a post-probation employee cannot be terminated without the consent of the authorities. During probation, consent is not required. For this reason, we recommend you set the probation period to the maximum allowed.

Please use a fixed-term of over 6 months (i.e not exactly 6 months) if you want to use a probation period. 6 months is not enough to have a valid probation.

salary_overview.title: Salary overview

helpCenter.content:
A reserve payment is an amount collected by Remote to help safeguard against potential large or unexpected severance costs if a team member's employment or engagement ends.

In many countries, labor laws require employers to pay statutory severance. Depending on the agreement, there may also be additional contractual obligations. Reserve payments help ensure funds are available to cover these costs if they arise.

Reserves are an industry-standard practice. Once a team member resigns or their agreement ends and all termination-related costs have been settled, any remaining reserve balance will be credited or refunded.

If a reserve payment has been made but onboarding is not completed, the full reserve will be credited or refunded. If your account has an overdue balance, Remote may first apply the reserve toward that outstanding amount.

Note: Reserve payments are required only for Employer of Record (EOR) employees and Contractor of Record (COR) contractors. They are not applicable to Global Payroll (direct employee) or users of our Standard Contractor Management and Contractor Management Plus platforms

Why would a reserve be required?

Remote evaluates several factors when determining whether a reserve payment is needed. These may include:

  • The financial exposure associated with a client’s account
  • The countries in which team members are hired
  • A client’s decision to move from 14-day to 30-day invoice payment terms
  • Non-standard employment contract terms, such as:
    • Extended notice periods
    • Guaranteed severance clauses
    • Seniority recognition
    • Non-compete, non-solicitation, or non-interference clauses
  • Consistent late invoice payments may also result in a reserve payment requirement

Why was I asked to pay an additional reserve?

Some employment agreement terms increase the potential cost of ending an agreement. In these cases, additional reserves may be required.

Currently, reserves are automatically applied for:

  • Extended notice periods
  • Seniority recognition
  • Non-compete, non-solicitation, or non-interference clauses

Other agreement terms may require additional review and could result in additional reserve requirements.

Extended notice period

Labor laws in each country define a minimum notice period for ending an agreement. If the notice period in the agreement is longer than the statutory minimum, an additional reserve will be required for the difference.

Example: The minimum notice period is one month, but you request a three-month notice period. In this case, an additional two-month reserve would be required.

Seniority recognition

A reserve will be automatically issued where two or more years of service is recognized.

As a general guideline:

  • 2-4 years of recognized seniority, a reserve equal to 1-month reserve is required
  • 4-5 years of recognized seniority, a reserve equal to 2-months is required
  • More than 5 years of recognized seniority is subject to further review

See also: 
When is a reserve refunded?
What is reserve payment in Contractor of Record?
helpCenter.title: What is a reserve payment?

x-rmt-schema-changelog.changelog: Fixed-term contracts are now blocked and the option removed when the employee's seniority date is recognized (has_seniority_date: yes), consistent with other countries using the contract_duration component, once the eor_seniority_block and eor_seniority_block_v2_ftc feature flags are enabled for the Netherlands. Employments created before the seniority block cutoff date are grandfathered and unaffected. Remote Admins can still override the block for approved exceptions. The contract_end_date nested-field reference under the Fixed Term option moves from nested_field to nested_fields (a list), matching every other country on this shared component. contract_duration_type no longer pre-fills a default value; the customer must actively choose an option.
x-rmt-schema-changelog.upgradePath: No action required for existing contracts. Once the Netherlands' batch-2 seniority-block flags are enabled, new contract-details submissions for employments with a recognized seniority date no longer accept fixed_term for contract_duration_type (only indefinite is valid) and contract_end_date is rejected if provided, unless the request is made by a Remote Admin.
